Subject: Live POC runbook & workshop scheduling - Acme Retail

Hi Sarah / Mark —

Thanks again for agreeing to a hands-on POC with Redwood. To make the session actionable, proposed agenda below (90–120 min):

- 10m quick goals & success criteria (confirm with Acme)
- 25m prompt review & input engineering (routing rules, function calls)
- 30m live inference demo with your sample prompts and dataset
- 20m controlled load tests (target 100–300 rps bursts)
- 15m wrap: notes, next steps, owners/timelines

Proposed dates/times (PT):
- Tue May 24, 10:00–12:00
- Wed May 25, 09:00–11:00

Attachments: runbook_v1.pdf (runbook + step checklist).

Ask: please confirm which slot works for Mark and whether you can share a small sample of expected prompt traffic (5–10 representative prompts) and a preferred token budget per request. That lets us pre-provision the correct instance profile and KV-cache rules.

I'll loop in Karthik and Monica from Solutions/Engineering once we lock a time.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: runbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]

Subject: Prep checklist + load test plan for Wed May 25 session

Folks —

Thanks for the heads up. I put together a lightweight prep checklist and a default load profile we can use if Acme’s CSV is delayed. Highlights:

- Runbook changes: add explicit fallback to t5-med (quantized) after 2s latency or 8 tokens/sec median; enable KV prefix cache for common prompts.
- Load profile (attached acme_load_profile.csv): 3 bursts during a 15‑minute window (10s ramp, 3 min sustain): 20 rps, 80 rps, 160 rps.
- Data/creds: Acme to provide a sample prompt file + one S3 read-only key for the sample dataset.
- Measurement: we’ll capture 95th/99th latency, token cost, and error rate per burst.

Attachments: acme_load_profile.csv

If Acme’s traffic looks different, we’ll swap to their CSV; the runbook is parametric.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Live POC — session recap, action items, and next steps

Hi Sarah / Mark —

Great session this morning — thanks for the active participation. Below is a short recap and owners for follow-ups. I’ve attached the recording and the annotated runbook.

Recap (high level):
- Walked through prompts and routing rules; confirmed prefix caching reduced repeated prompt latency by ~25% on test set.
- Load tests: ran two bursts (80 rps and 160 rps). 95th latency stayed under 450ms for the lower model; the fallback model activation triggered as expected for the 160 rps burst (increased token efficiency, slightly higher latency).
- Observed a small error spike during the last minute of the 160 rps burst — suspected transient S3 rate limiting for the sample dataset reads.

Action items:
- Acme: provide final prompt set + 1-week anonymized sample traffic CSV (owner: Sarah) — due 2027-05-28
- Redwood (Monica): adjust demo cluster to use NVMe cache permanently for the PoC and add a circuit-breaker metric for S3 read errors — due 2027-05-27
- Redwood (Karthik): finalize runbook with explicit fallback thresholds and cost notes; share a versioned PDF — due 2027-05-26
- Dylan: schedule follow-up deep-dive on model selection and cost tradeoffs (60 min) — propose Wed Jun 2 or Thu Jun 3

Attachments: session_recording_20270524.mp4, updated_runbook_v1-1.pdf

Please reply with availability for the follow-up (Jun 2 or Jun 3) and confirm the owners/due dates above.

Thanks again — excited to move forward.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: session_recording_20270524.mp4 (MP4, 43MB)]
